unit.title: Position and Transformation
unit.blurb: Bearings, the midpoint of a line segment, and translations, reflections, rotations and enlargements on a coordinate grid.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Understand and use bearings as a measure of direction.

O2.t: Find the midpoint of a line segment from the coordinates of its end points.

O3.t: Translate shapes using vectors written as column vectors.

O4.t: Reflect shapes in horizontal, vertical and diagonal mirror lines, including y = x.

O5.t: Rotate shapes about a centre through 90° and 180°.

O6.t: Enlarge shapes by a positive scale factor from a centre of enlargement.

p: A **bearing** gives a direction as an angle measured **clockwise from north**. It always has **three figures**: east is 090°, south is 180°, west is 270°.
The bearing of A from B is measured at B.
If the bearing of B from A is θ, the bearing of A from B is θ + 180° (or θ − 180° if θ is 180° or more).

Explain why the bearing of A from B is 180° more than the bearing of B from A when the first bearing is less than 180°.
req.model: Going from B back to A is the exact opposite direction, and opposite directions differ by 180°. So you add 180° (or subtract it if the bearing is 180° or more).
req.reason: Going from B back to A is the exact opposite direction, and opposite directions differ by 180°. So you add 180° (or subtract it if the bearing is 180° or more).

sections.title: The midpoint of a line segment

p: The **midpoint** is halfway along a line segment. Find the **mean of the x-coordinates** and the **mean of the y-coordinates**.
Add the x-coordinates (do not subtract), then divide by 2.

p: A **translation** slides a shape without turning it. A **column vector** (a over b) means move **a** right (left if negative) and **b** up (down if negative).
Every point moves the same way, so the image is congruent to the object.
In (a over b), the TOP number moves left or right; the BOTTOM number moves up or down.

p: In a **reflection** each image point is the same distance from the mirror line as the object point, on the other side.
Reflect in the **x-axis**: (x, y) → (x, −y). In the **y-axis**: (x, y) → (−x, y). In **y = x**: (x, y) → (y, x).
Measure distances to the mirror line at right angles to it, especially for diagonal mirror lines.

p: An **enlargement** changes the size of a shape. Every length is multiplied by the **scale factor**; angles do not change.
From a **centre of enlargement**, each image point is (scale factor) times as far from the centre as the object point.
Scale factor 2 doubles every length, but the area becomes 4 times as big.
